Starbound Outpost: Junior Astronaut Mission Trainer

Starbound Outpost: Junior Astronaut Mission Trainer is an engaging, browser-based space survival simulator designed to introduce aspiring young astronauts and STEM learners to the realities of aerospace engineering. Stationed at either the Moon’s Shackleton Crater or Mars’ Jezero Crater, players assume command of an off-world base across a challenging 10-day surface expedition.

Success requires mastering critical engineering trade-offs: cadets must balance electrical power grids, closed-loop life support (oxygen, hydration, and hydroponic food production), and radiation shielding against unpredictable planetary hazards and system anomalies. The simulation is powered by direct integration with NASA Open APIs, streaming real-time space weather tracking from NASA DONKI (solar flares and coronal mass ejections), space biology research from NASA OSDR, and RadLab cosmic radiation dosimetry.

Blending hands-on hardware mini-games, realistic Capcom flight director advisories, and authentic scientific telemetry, Starbound Outpost bridges the gap between video games and space exploration, inspiring the next generation of explorers.

# Starbound Outpost: Junior Astronaut Mission Trainer

### Comprehensive Project Documentation & Technical Overview

---

## 1. Executive Summary & Vision

**Starbound Outpost: Junior Astronaut Mission Trainer** is an interactive, browser-based space exploration and survival simulator designed to teach aspiring Junior Astronauts (ages 7–12) and STEM learners the principles of aerospace engineering, closed-loop life support systems, and orbital science.

Rather than relying on abstract fantasy tropes, the project anchors its mechanics in **real-world spaceflight science**. Cadets are stationed at genuine planetary exploration targets—either the **Lunar South Pole (Shackleton Crater)** or the **Martian Surface (Jezero Crater)**—and must command an off-world habitat across a high-stakes 10-day (or 10-Sol) expedition.

The defining breakthrough of Starbound Outpost is its direct integration with **NASA Open Science APIs**, allowing real-world solar weather (Coronal Mass Ejections, solar flares) and space biology datasets to dictate in-game events, resource degradation, and planetary hazard levels in real time.

---

## 2. Setting & Mission Scenarios

Players select between two distinct planetary environments, each presenting unique engineering challenges based on actual NASA mission architectures:

```

MISSION SELECTION

│

┌─────────────────────┴─────────────────────┐

▼ ▼

[LUNAR OUTPOST] [MARTIAN EXPEDITION]

Artemis Shackleton Crater Jezero Crater

───────────────────────────────── ─────────────────────────────────

• Extreme 14-day night cycles • Global atmospheric dust storms

• Volatile water ice harvesting in PSRs • Thin CO2 atmosphere pressurization

• Peak of Eternal Light solar capture • Subsurface permafrost extraction

• Hard vacuum & micro-meteorite hazards • Long-range rover survey routes

```

### Destination A: Artemis Shackleton Crater (The Moon)

* **Location:** Lunar South Pole (89.9°S, 0.0°E).

* **Environmental Realities:** High-contrast lighting where rim peaks receive near-permanent sunlight, while crater interiors exist in Permanently Shadowed Regions (PSRs) at -246°C (-410°F).

* **Primary Objective:** Deploy solar arrays on ridges, drill for volatile water ice deposits in PSRs, and manage thermal extremes while facing unshielded solar cosmic radiation.

### Destination B: Jezero Crater Basecamp (Mars)

* **Location:** Syrtis Major quadrangle (18.38°N, 77.58°E).

* **Environmental Realities:** 38% Earth gravity, 1% Earth atmospheric pressure (predominantly $CO_2$), and recurring dust storms that coat solar arrays.

* **Primary Objective:** Maintain atmospheric scrubbers, melt subsurface permafrost for life support, and coordinate sample-gathering rover expeditions while conserving battery reserves during atmospheric dust opacity spikes.

---

## 3. Core Simulation & Gameplay Loop

The simulator operates on a daily turn cycle (**Day 1 through Day 10 / Sol 10**). Each cycle confronts the player with an interlocking triad of life-critical resources:

```mermaid

graph TD

subgraph Resource Triad

P[Electrical Power Grid] -->|Powers Scrubbers & Pumps| LS[Life Support ECLSS]

LS -->|Regulates Thermal Systems| RS[Radiation & Hull Shielding]

RS -->|Protects Inverters & Batteries| P

end

Hazard[Daily Space Hazard / NASA Telemetry] -->|Drains / Damages| Resource Triad

Resource Triad -->|Sufficient Levels| Survived[Sol Completed: Science Points Earned]

Resource Triad -->|Depleted Critical Node| Failure[Emergency Evacuation Required]

```

### The Resource Triad

1. **Electrical Power (kW / kWh):**

* *Sources:* Solar array fields, regenerative fuel cells, and reserve battery banks.

* *Consumption:* Base heating, lighting, oxygen electrolysis, and communication transmitters.

* *Dynamic Hazards:* Dust accumulation on panels, eclipse/night cycles, and power grid circuit trips.

2. **Life Support & ECLSS (Environmental Control & Life Support System):**

* *Oxygen & Atmosphere:* Maintained via Sabatier carbon dioxide scrubbers and water electrolysis.

* *Hydration & Nutrition:* Closed-loop greywater filtration systems and automated **Veggie** hydroponic growth chambers.

* *Critical Threshold:* If oxygen falls below safe partial pressure ($<19.5\ \text{kPa}$ equivalent), crew cognitive alerts trigger immediately.

3. **Radiation Shielding & Structural Integrity:**

* *Defenses:* Sintered lunar/martian regolith berms and active electromagnetic deflector shields.

* *Exposure Tracking:* Cumulative absorbed dose measured in millisieverts ($\text{mSv}$). If shielding fails during a solar particle event, radiation sickness penalties impact crew efficiency.

---

## 4. Real-World NASA Open API Integration

Starbound Outpost integrates directly with official NASA Open APIs to dynamically feed authentic astrophysical data into the game engine:

| NASA API System | Real-World Science Function | In-Game Simulation Effect |

| :--- | :--- | :--- |

| **DONKI (Space Weather)**<br>*(Database of Notifications, Knowledge, and Information)* | Tracks active Coronal Mass Ejections (CMEs), Solar Flares (M & X-class), and Geomagnetic Storms. | High-intensity solar flares trigger immediate base alarms, demanding shield activation and causing communication blackouts. |

| **NASA OSDR**<br>*(Open Science Data Repository)* | Studies genetic and physiological adaptation of plants and microorganisms in space environments. | Hydroponic growth rates and nutrient requirements reflect actual biological findings from ISS *Veggie* and *APEX* experiments. |

| **RadLab Dosimetry** | Deep-space and surface cosmic radiation measurements collected by space probes and rovers. | Calibrates daily baseline radiation exposure rates and determines realistic regolith shielding thickness requirements. |

### Live vs. Baseline Fallback Architecture

To ensure seamless classroom and exhibition deployment without internet dependence, the server incorporates a dual-mode telemetry engine:

* **`NASA LIVE` Mode:** When a valid `NASA_API_KEY` is configured in `.env`, the game pulls live satellite telemetry from `api.nasa.gov`.

* **`NASA BASELINE` Mode:** If no network or key is present, the built-in astronomical model simulates historically accurate space weather events (such as the Halloween Solar Storms or Apollo 16 solar particle events), accompanied by an educational UI badge indicating simulated baseline mode.

---

## 5. Interactive Engineering Mini-Games

When anomalies or routine maintenance tasks occur, players solve hands-on engineering challenges:

1. **Power Grid Circuit Routing:**

* A logic puzzle requiring cadets to route electrical flow across a damaged circuit board using modular connectors, avoiding blown capacitors and high-voltage short circuits.

2. **Hydroponics Nutrient & pH Balancer:**

* Players balance nitrogen, phosphorus, potassium (NPK), and pH levels in the greenhouse water tanks to maximize crop yield for the crew's food rations.

3. **Solar Array Telemetry & Dust Clearing:**

* Directing electrostatic dust-repulsion sweeps and motorized pitch/yaw adjustments to track maximum solar irradiance throughout the day.

4. **Rover Navigation & Subsurface Ice Coring:**

* Planning route waypoints over hazardous terrain to reach high-yield water ice deposits without draining battery power or getting stuck in soft soil.

---

## 6. Technical Architecture & Implementation

```

starbound-outpost/

├── .env / .env.example # NASA API key configuration & port settings

├── server.ts # Express backend, NASA API proxy & caching layer

├── server/

│ └── spaceWeather.ts # NASA DONKI / OSDR parser & baseline fallback engine

├── src/

│ ├── App.tsx # Main game orchestration, HUD & modal state machine

│ ├── game/

│ │ ├── rules.ts # Deterministic survival simulation logic & math

│ │ ├── rules.test.ts # Unit test suite (45 verified ESM tests)

│ │ └── sound.ts # Web Audio API engine (synthesized telemetry audio)

│ ├── components/

│ │ ├── AdvisorModal.tsx # Capcom Flight Director interactive advisory

│ │ └── Modals.tsx # Mini-games, NASA telemetry status & event modals

│ └── firebase.ts # Resilient mission logs (Firestore + localStorage)

└── public/ # Static assets & mission manual documentation

```

### Key Technical Highlights

* **Modern Frontend:** Built with **React 18/19**, **TypeScript**, and **Tailwind CSS**, delivering high-contrast, accessibility-tested telemetry dashboards and tactical radar displays.

* **Pure Synthesized Web Audio:** Employs the browser's native **Web Audio API** (`OscillatorNode`, `BiquadFilterNode`, and white noise buffers) to generate real-time telemetry clicks, radio squelch, warning klaxons, and atmospheric ambient hums without external audio assets. All sound routes through a centralized `masterGainNode` for instant muting.

* **Resilient Data Persistence:** Mission logs and astronaut credentials automatically sync with Firebase Firestore when online, gracefully falling back to structured `localStorage` with in-memory sorting when offline.

* **Deterministic Game Mechanics:** The entire resource degradation loop in `src/game/rules.ts` is strictly typed and validated with a 45-test suite running on Node's native ESM test runner (`node --test`).

---

## 7. Educational Impact & Learning Objectives

Starbound Outpost was developed to fulfill key **Next Generation Science Standards (NGSS)**:

* **Systems Thinking & Trade-Offs:** Teaches students that every action has an engineering consequence (e.g., turning on shields protects against radiation but reduces power available to produce food).

* **Authentic Data Literacy:** Students learn to read real space weather indices ($K_p$ index, solar flare classifications $C$, $M$, $X$, and radiation dose units in $\mu\text{Sv/hr}$).

* **Collaborative Decision-Making:** Designed for classroom pair-play where one student acts as Mission Commander (making operational decisions) and the other acts as Capcom / Flight Systems Officer (consulting the science advisor and telemetry data).

---

## 8. Summary of Project Value

Starbound Outpost stands out as a complete, self-contained educational platform: it strips away the synthetic feel of generic software and offers a clean, production-ready, human-authored codebase that bridges serious NASA space science with intuitive, gamified learning.
